title: Top pay outran the middle on overtime; City-funded nonprofits paid bonuses in hard years

beats.text: Take San Francisco’s 100 highest-paid employees.

visual.label: average pay, the 100 highest-paid City employees

beats.text: In fiscal 2013, they averaged 277,570 dollars.

visual.label: average pay, the 100 highest-paid City employees

beats.text: By fiscal 2026?

visual.label: average pay, the 100 highest-paid City employees

beats.text: 562,109 dollars.
This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: What changed? Overtime. It was 17 percent of their pay. Now it’s 44 percent.

a: overtime, share of top-100 pay, fiscal 2013

beats.text: Overtime is pay for hours worked, so it isn’t a bonus.

visual.line: set by who works the most extra hours, not by the pay scale

beats.text: But the top City paychecks are now set by who works the most extra hours.

visual.line: set by who works the most extra hours, not by the pay scale

beats.text: Then a payroll column called other pay: premiums, incentives, one-time payments. In fiscal 2026 it came to?

visual.label: Other pay
visual.sub: premium pay, incentive pay, other one-time payments

beats.text: 282.5 million dollars.
In Police, it went from 19.1 million dollars to 63.2 million.
What is it? The file doesn’t say.

visual.line: wage increases, retention pay, step adjustments, and signing bonus

beats.text: The budget analyst noted the 2023 police deal brought retention pay and a signing bonus.

visual.line: wage increases, retention pay, step adjustments, and signing bonus

beats.text: Against 12 county payrolls, though, San Francisco’s other pay and lump sums,

visual.label: 12 county payrolls
visual.sub: other pay plus lump sums, share of regular pay, 2024

beats.text: 5.4 percent of regular pay in 2024, rank 10 of 13.

visual.label: Other pay plus lump sums, share of regular pay, 2024

beats.text: Not large, by California standards.
Other pay topped a whole year’s salary 1,411 times since 2017.

visual.label: times other pay topped a whole year’s salary

beats.text: The largest: 329,750 dollars, to Mark Gonzales,
a deputy chief in the Fire Department, in 2019.
Most are unused leave, paid out on leaving: money already earned.

visual.line: a payout of unused leave on leaving: money already earned

beats.text: The ones worth a look went to people who stayed.

visual.line: a payout of unused leave on leaving: money already earned

beats.text: Now City-funded nonprofits. The Controller’s rules bar charging City contracts for staff bonuses.

visual.text: Costs that may not be charged to the City include “Bonuses paid to staff.” One Controller audit, 2022 to 2026: “More Than $200,000 in Bonuses Were Unplanned and Paid”.

beats.text: Where the City gives a quarter or more of the money, how much in bonuses?

visual.label: City money, a quarter or more of revenue

beats.text: 4.6 million dollars.
The largest: 198,400 dollars,
to Karen J Hanrahan, chief executive of Glide Foundation, in 2023.

visual.label: Glide Foundation
visual.sub: Karen J Hanrahan, President/CEO, year ended 30 June 2023

beats.text: The City gave Glide 33 percent of its revenue.

visual.label: Glide Foundation
visual.sub: Karen J Hanrahan, President/CEO, year ended 30 June 2023

beats.text: Not City money, say the rules. Which money, the return doesn’t say.
Reporting the most: Low Income Investment Fund, and Meals On Wheels.
And 68 times, a top officer got a bonus or a big raise in a hard year.

visual.label: bonuses or big raises for a top officer in a hard year

beats.text: A deficit, lost staff, or audit findings.

visual.label: bonuses or big raises for a top officer in a hard year

visual.label: Main Street Launch
visual.sub: year ended 30 June 2024; employees down from 20 to 17
visual.chip: $3.1 million more spent than taken in

beats.text: Nothing shows a bonus came from City money, or what other pay was, for anyone.

cards: That any bonus was paid from City money
What “other pay” is for any person

beats.text: What would settle it? The pay codes behind other pay, and the leave balance behind each big payout.

cards.what: The pay codes behind the “other salaries” column
Leave balances behind each large payout

beats.text: Nothing here has been ruled on by any authority. And high pay is not misconduct.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
